---
title: "Read NSS 68 data from the MoSPI portal"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# pkgdown renders from vignettes/articles/, so the data goes to vignettes/articles/data
id <- "DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-68Rnd-Sch2.0-July2011-June2012"
data_dir <- file.path("data", id)
rar_file <- file.path(data_dir, "Nss68_1.0_Type2_new format.rar")
stata_zip <- file.path(
  data_dir, "STATA_data_nss68_consumer_expenditure_type2.zip"
)
have_files <- file.exists(rar_file) && file.exists(stata_zip)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = have_files || nzchar(Sys.getenv("MOSPI_KEY")))
```

```{r no-key, eval=!knitr::opts_chunk$get("eval"), echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
cat(
  "> There was no `MOSPI_KEY` when this article was built.",
  "Thus, the article shows the code without output.\n"
)
```

This article uses the Household Consumer Expenditure Survey of NSS round 68
(July 2011 to June 2012), Schedule 1.0 Type 2.
We do these steps:

1. Download the `.rar` archive and the Stata files with
   [mospiR](https://mospir.saketlab.org).
2. Extract the `.Nesstar` file from the archive.
3. Read the `.Nesstar` file with nesstarR.
4. Calculate the mean household expenditure on cereals.
5. Compare each dataset with the Stata file from the portal.

The packages mospiR, archive and haven do the download, the extraction and
the Stata import.

## Download the files

You must have an API key for the
[MoSPI Microdata Portal](https://microdata.gov.in).
Set the environment variable `MOSPI_KEY` in `~/.Renviron`.

The dataset has 27 files. We download only two files:

- `Nss68_1.0_Type2_new format.rar` (67 MB) contains the `.Nesstar` file.
- `STATA_data_nss68_consumer_expenditure_type2.zip` (151 MB) contains the
  same data as Stata files.

```{r download, eval=FALSE}
library(mospiR)
api_key <- Sys.getenv("MOSPI_KEY")
id <- "DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSSO-68Rnd-Sch2.0-July2011-June2012"
data_dir <- file.path("data", id)

files <- list_files(id, api_key)
for (f in c(
  "Nss68_1.0_Type2_new format.rar",
  "STATA_data_nss68_consumer_expenditure_type2.zip"
)) {
  download_file(id, f, data_dir, api_key, .files_cache = files)
}
```

```{r download-if-missing, ref.label="download", include=FALSE, eval=!have_files && nzchar(Sys.getenv("MOSPI_KEY"))}
```

## Extract the archive

`archive::archive_extract()` extracts `.rar` archives on all platforms.
The archive contains the `.Nesstar` file, a DDI XML file and documents.

```{r extract}
nesstar_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "nesstar")
if (!dir.exists(nesstar_dir)) {
  archive::archive_extract(
    file.path(data_dir, "Nss68_1.0_Type2_new format.rar"),
    dir = nesstar_dir
  )
}
nesstar_path <- list.files(nesstar_dir,
  pattern = "[.]Nesstar$",
  recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE
)
basename(nesstar_path)
file.size(nesstar_path) / 1e9
```

The `.Nesstar` file is approximately 1.5 GB.

## Parse the file

`nesstar_parse()` decodes the resource index, the dataset descriptors and
the variable directories. It does not decode row data, and it does not keep
the file in memory. The other functions read only the bytes that they need
from the file.

```{r parse}
library(nesstarR)
nb <- nesstar_parse(nesstar_path)
nb
```

## List the datasets

The file has one dataset for each level of the schedule.

```{r datasets}
ds_tbl <- nesstar_datasets(nb)
ds_tbl
```

## Read the labels

This file does not contain the XML blocks with the labels.
Thus, `nesstar_metadata()` gives a warning and returns `NULL`.
The labels are in the file `ddi.xml` in the archive.

```{r metadata}
meta <- nesstar_metadata(nb)
is.null(meta)
```

## Read the item-level dataset

The dataset with the most rows has one row for each household and item.

```{r items}
item_ds <- ds_tbl$dataset_number[which.max(ds_tbl$row_count)]
nesstar_variables(nb, dataset_number = item_ds)$name
```

To decode only some columns, use the `columns` argument.

```{r read}
items <- nesstar_read_dataset(
  nb,
  dataset_number = item_ds,
  columns = c(
    "HHID", "Sector", "Item_Code",
    "Total_Consumption_Value", "Combined_Multiplier"
  )
)
dim(items)
head(items)
```

## Calculate the expenditure on cereals

Item code 129 is the sub-total for cereals (item codes 101 to 122).
`Total_Consumption_Value` is in rupees.
`Combined_Multiplier` is the household weight.
In `Sector`, 1 is rural and 2 is urban.

Some households have no row for item 129. For these households, the
expenditure on cereals is 0.

```{r cereals}
hh <- items[!duplicated(items$HHID), c("HHID", "Sector", "Combined_Multiplier")]
cereals <- items[items$Item_Code == "129", c("HHID", "Total_Consumption_Value")]
hh <- merge(hh, cereals, by = "HHID", all.x = TRUE)
hh$Total_Consumption_Value[is.na(hh$Total_Consumption_Value)] <- 0

nrow(hh)
weighted_total <- rowsum(hh$Total_Consumption_Value * hh$Combined_Multiplier, hh$Sector)
weight <- rowsum(hh$Combined_Multiplier, hh$Sector)
round(weighted_total / weight, 1)
```

## Export to CSV

`nesstar_export()` writes each dataset to a different CSV file. By default,
it reads 50,000 rows at a time and writes gzip files.
This example writes only the first dataset.

```{r export}
out <- nesstar_export(nb,
  output_dir = tempdir(),
  datasets = ds_tbl$dataset_number[1]
)
basename(out)
```

```{r cleanup-items, include=FALSE}
rm(items, hh, cereals)
invisible(gc())
```

## Compare with the Stata files

The portal also supplies the data as Stata files.
We compare each Stata file with the related dataset in the `.Nesstar` file.
The file has no labels, so we cannot match the datasets by name.
Thus, we match each Stata file to the dataset with the same number of rows
and columns.

```{r stata-unzip}
stata_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "stata")
if (!dir.exists(stata_dir)) unzip(stata_zip, exdir = stata_dir)
dta_files <- list.files(stata_dir,
  pattern = "[.]dta$",
  recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE
)
length(dta_files)
```

`nesstar_compare()` compares one dataset with a data frame from a different
source. It matches the columns by name and ignores differences in
punctuation, for example `Srl._No.` and `Srl_No`. Refer to
`?nesstar_compare` for the full rules.
`haven::zap_labels()` removes the value labels from the Stata data before the
comparison.

The code reads one Stata file and one dataset at a time to limit the
memory use.

```{r compare}
results <- data.frame()
for (f in dta_files) {
  s <- as.data.frame(haven::zap_labels(haven::read_dta(f)))
  hit <- ds_tbl$dataset_number[ds_tbl$row_count == nrow(s) &
    ds_tbl$variable_count == ncol(s)]
  row <- data.frame(
    stata_file = basename(f), dataset = NA_integer_,
    rows = nrow(s), columns = ncol(s),
    unmatched_columns = NA_integer_, different_values = NA_integer_
  )
  if (length(hit) == 1) {
    cmp <- nesstar_compare(nb, dataset_number = hit, reference = s)
    row$dataset <- hit
    row$unmatched_columns <- sum(is.na(cmp$different_values))
    row$different_values <- sum(cmp$different_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  results <- rbind(results, row)
  rm(s)
  invisible(gc())
}
results[order(results$dataset), ]
```

Each Stata file must match one dataset. Each column must be in the two
sources, and all values must be equal.

```{r compare-check}
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(results$dataset),
  all(results$unmatched_columns == 0),
  all(results$different_values == 0)
)
```
